observation_summary: The ValueMarker constructor was incorrectly passing the 'paint' and 'stroke' arguments to the superclass constructor instead of the 'outlinePaint' and 'outlineStroke' arguments, causing the marker to be initialized with the wrong colors and strokes.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the arguments passed to the superclass constructor in the ValueMarker class. This is a classic case of incorrect initialization where the wrong variables were used to set the object's state. It is not an algorithmic error, nor a missing check, nor a design-level capability issue.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the constructor call 'super(paint, stroke, paint, stroke, alpha);' being changed to 'super(paint, stroke, outlinePaint, outlineStroke, alpha);'.
The failing test indicates that the outline paint was expected to be blue but was red, confirming that the wrong paint was assigned during initialization.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a change in procedural logic or computation, but rather a correction of the values passed to an initialization method.
While it involves a method call, the issue is not a mismatch in the interface contract between components, but an internal error in how the object initializes its own state using its superclass.
